rules.title: Primitive integer/float sizes and alignments
rules.statement: Scalar layout {size,align} in bytes: bool/i8/u8 = {1,1}; i16/u16 = {2,2}; i24/u24 = {3,1}; i32/u32/f32/char/{integer literal} = {4,4}; i56/u56 = {7,1}; i64/u64/f64/{float literal} = {8,8}; i128/u128 = {16,16}. usize/isize and all pointers are target-pointer-width-sized (8 on a 64-bit target).
rules.divergence: A: Logos adds non-power-of-two integer widths i24/u24 (align 1) and i56/u56 (align 1) not present in Rust.
rules.uncertainty: Odd-width align=1 inferred from the literal {3,1}/{7,1} entries.

rules.title: Unit and never are zero-sized
rules.statement: The unit type () (Void) and the never type ! (Never) have layout {size=0, align=1}. As a struct/enum field each occupies a zero-size slot ([i8;0]) so sibling field offsets are unaffected; in value/result position they yield no SSA value.

rules.title: Fat pointers are 16 bytes, pointer-aligned
rules.statement: Slice (&[T], str), closure value, trait object (dyn), and custom-DST reference each have layout {size=16, align=8}: a two-word fat pair (data + metadata). The metadata word is length for slices/custom-DST and a vtable pointer for trait objects; closures pair {fn, env}.

rules.title: Unsized pointees have no by-value footprint
rules.statement: Unsized types — the slice pointee [T] (UnsizedSlice) and the dyn pointee (UnsizedDyn) — have layout {size=0, align=1}; they have no by-value representation and may only appear behind a pointer/reference.

rules.title: Array layout = N x element
rules.statement: An array [T; N] has size = N * size_of(T) and align = align_of(T), where T's element representation is its full inline by-value footprint (struct/enum/slice/closure/dyn/tuple elements are embedded inline, not collapsed to a pointer).

rules.title: Struct/tuple layout = ordered fields with natural padding
rules.statement: A struct or tuple lays out fields in declaration order: each field starts at the next offset rounded up to its alignment, the aggregate's align = max(field aligns), and total size = accumulated offset rounded up to the aggregate align. All aggregate members are embedded inline by value.

rules.title: #[repr(transparent)] inherits the single field's layout
rules.statement: A #[repr(transparent)] struct with exactly one field has layout identical to that field's layout (no added aggregate padding/alignment). Multi-field #[repr(transparent)] is rejected earlier (collect time), so the single-field invariant holds.

rules.title: Union layout = max size / max align
rules.statement: A union's size = round_up(max(field sizes), align) and align = max(field aligns); all fields overlap at offset 0 (share field index 0). The physical body is {<largest-aligned field type>, [pad x i8]} so the aggregate's own align = max-align and raw size = max-size.

rules.title: Tagged enum layout = {i32 disc, aligned payload}
rules.statement: A tagged (data-carrying) enum has layout = aggregate of a 4-byte/4-align discriminant followed by the payload blob {payload_bytes, payload_align}: the payload starts at round_up(4, payload_align) and total size rounds up to the enum align. The payload is sized from the concrete instantiation so nested generics (e.g. Option<Option<i64>>) carry their full inline footprint.

rules.title: C-like enum is a backing-type-sized discriminant
rules.statement: A fieldless (C-like) enum has no payload; its layout is a single discriminant whose size = ceil(disc_bits/8) bytes (min 1) with equal alignment, where disc_bits is the enum's backing integer width.

rules.title: Aggregate fields are embedded by value, references inline as fat pairs
rules.statement: A struct field whose type is a struct, tuple, tagged enum, slice, closure, custom-DST ref, or bare dyn trait object is embedded inline by value (the struct/enum's aggregate type, or its 16-byte fat pair, occupies the field). A field that is a pointer/reference to such a type (e.g. *Struct, &Struct, *const dyn) stores an 8-byte thin pointer instead.

rules.title: AnyVal is a 4-byte i32 everywhere
rules.statement: The AnyVal type is uniformly represented as a scalar i32 (size/align {4,4}) in every position — value, argument, and struct field — never as a wrapped aggregate.

rules.title: char is a 32-bit value
rules.statement: char is a 32-bit (4-byte, 4-align) value, representing a Unicode scalar.

rules.title: Reference representation classified by outer kind
rules.statement: A reference's thin/fat representation is determined by its outermost kind, not its pointee: raw/safe pointers (*T, &T, *mut T to sized), fn pointers, and fn items are thin (8-byte); slice/dyn/closure values are fat (16-byte); a pointer wrapping an unsized pointee (e.g. *const dyn) stays thin while a bare dyn value is the fat pair. A self-describing custom-DST ref is physically thin (8-byte) since its tail length is in-band.

rules.title: &mut to a #[zone_mut] type is a fat zone-carrying ref
rules.statement: A &mut T where T is a #[zone_mut] struct is a fat reference {data, zone} carrying its allocator/zone pointer, so growth methods reach the allocator through &mut self. A shared &T or *T to the same type stays thin (reads never grow).
rules.divergence: Logos addition: zone-carrying mutable references (Writ/zone model), no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: #[rel_ptr] and #[zoned2] pointers are stored self-relative
rules.statement: A #[rel_ptr] struct is represented as a self-relative pointer: 8-byte i64 offset storage, resolved to an absolute thin pointer on access. Additionally, a thin-pointer field of a #[zoned2] struct is stored self-relative (offset) rather than absolute.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: self-relative pointer storage (persistent/Writ model), no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Niche-packed enum carries no discriminant word
rules.statement: A niche-optimized (niche-packed) enum has no separate discriminant word: its representation is the niche-bearing payload alone, with layout {payload_bytes, payload_align} (pointer-sized when the niche field is a pointer). The active variant is distinguished by an in-payload niche value rather than a stored tag. A non-niche tagged enum instead carries an explicit discriminant word ({i32 disc, aligned payload}).
rules.divergence: Rust-conformant in intent (niche optimization); see ref_enum_niche.
